spec.title: Q3 2026 Treasury Liquidity Assessment
spec.subtitle: Ref: TR-26-118 | Date: 7 August 2026 | From: Group Treasury Department

sections.heading: Executive Overview
sections.body: As of 31 July 2026, consolidated cash and cash equivalents totalled USD 428.6 million, reflecting disciplined forecasting and conservative outflow assumptions for the remainder of the quarter. Net operating inflows for July exceeded plan by 4.2%, primarily due to earlier-than-expected collections in the North American segment. Based on current projections, minimum month-end liquidity through September 2026 is expected to remain above USD 310 million, comfortably above the Board-approved floor of USD 250 million.

sections.heading: Short-Term Funding Sources
sections.body: The Group maintains diversified short-term funding lines comprising USD 200 million in committed revolving credit facilities, EUR 90 million in bilateral overdrafts, and a USD 75 million commercial paper program. As of the reporting date, commercial paper outstanding stands at USD 32 million with weighted average maturity of 41 days. No bilateral overdrafts are currently drawn. Treasury has staggered maturities to ensure that no more than USD 50 million falls due within any rolling 14-day period.

sections.heading: Credit Facility Utilisation
sections.body: Total utilisation of committed revolving facilities is 38%, equivalent to USD 76 million drawn under the syndicated RCF maturing in March 2029. Headroom under committed lines therefore amounts to USD 124 million, excluding ancillary facilities. All covenant tests as of 30 June 2026 were passed with significant cushion, including net leverage at 2.1x versus a covenant threshold of 3.5x. No waivers or amendments are anticipated for the current quarter.

sections.heading: Foreign Exchange Exposure
sections.body: Forecast transactional FX exposure for Q3 2026 is primarily concentrated in EUR and GBP revenues against a USD reporting base. Net exposure over the next three months is estimated at EUR 54 million and GBP 22 million. Treasury has hedged 72% of forecast EUR exposure and 65% of GBP exposure using forward contracts with maturities aligned to projected cash receipts. A 10% adverse movement in both currencies would reduce EBITDA by approximately USD 6.4 million on an unhedged basis; after hedging, the residual impact is limited to USD 1.9 million.

sections.heading: Liquidity Stress Scenarios
sections.body: Stress testing was conducted under three scenarios: (i) 15% revenue shortfall, (ii) 60-day delay in receivables collection for two major customers, and (iii) simultaneous FX depreciation of 12% in EUR and GBP. Under the combined severe case, minimum projected liquidity declines to USD 268 million in mid-September, remaining above the internal threshold. Management action levers—including suspension of discretionary capex (USD 35 million) and temporary reduction in share repurchases—provide additional buffer if required.

structure.full_text:
Q3 2026 Treasury Liquidity Assessment
Ref: TR-26-118 | Date: 7 August 2026 | From: Group Treasury Department

Section Executive Overview
As of 31 July 2026, consolidated cash and cash equivalents totalled USD 428.6 million, reflecting disciplined forecasting and conservative outflow assumptions for the remainder of the quarter. Net operating inflows for July exceeded plan by 4.2%, primarily due to earlier-than-expected collections in the North American segment. Based on current projections, minimum month-end liquidity through September 2026 is expected to remain above USD 310 million, comfortably above the Board-approved floor of USD 250 million.

Section Short-Term Funding Sources
The Group maintains diversified short-term funding lines comprising USD 200 million in committed revolving credit facilities, EUR 90 million in bilateral overdrafts, and a USD 75 million commercial paper program. As of the reporting date, commercial paper outstanding stands at USD 32 million with weighted average maturity of 41 days. No bilateral overdrafts are currently drawn. Treasury has staggered maturities to ensure that no more than USD 50 million falls due within any rolling 14-day period.

Section Credit Facility Utilisation
Total utilisation of committed revolving facilities is 38%, equivalent to USD 76 million drawn under the syndicated RCF maturing in March 2029. Headroom under committed lines therefore amounts to USD 124 million, excluding ancillary facilities. All covenant tests as of 30 June 2026 were passed with significant cushion, including net leverage at 2.1x versus a covenant threshold of 3.5x. No waivers or amendments are anticipated for the current quarter.

Section Foreign Exchange Exposure
Forecast transactional FX exposure for Q3 2026 is primarily concentrated in EUR and GBP revenues against a USD reporting base. Net exposure over the next three months is estimated at EUR 54 million and GBP 22 million. Treasury has hedged 72% of forecast EUR exposure and 65% of GBP exposure using forward contracts with maturities aligned to projected cash receipts. A 10% adverse movement in both currencies would reduce EBITDA by approximately USD 6.4 million on an unhedged basis; after hedging, the residual impact is limited to USD 1.9 million.

Section Liquidity Stress Scenarios
Stress testing was conducted under three scenarios: (i) 15% revenue shortfall, (ii) 60-day delay in receivables collection for two major customers, and (iii) simultaneous FX depreciation of 12% in EUR and GBP. Under the combined severe case, minimum projected liquidity declines to USD 268 million in mid-September, remaining above the internal threshold. Management action levers—including suspension of discretionary capex (USD 35 million) and temporary reduction in share repurchases—provide additional buffer if required.

Confidential — Internal Distribution Only | Page 1 of 1

structure.heading: Credit Facilities, FX Exposure, and Liquidity Stress Scenarios for Q3 2026
text_content: **Credit Facilities, FX Exposure, and Liquidity Stress Scenarios for Q3 2026**

The Group’s committed Revolving Credit Facility (RCF) remains USD 500.0m, with USD 120.0m drawn and USD 10.0m in letters of credit outstanding as of 30 Jun 2026, representing a utilisation rate of 24.0% and contingent utilisation of 2.0%. Available undrawn capacity is USD 370.0m. All covenant metrics are currently within tested limits; near‑term refinancing and accordion options are reviewed monthly.

Net transactional FX exposure entering Q3 2026 is EUR 65.0m and GBP 40.0m as of 30 Jun 2026. The treasury plan deploys a layered hedging approach: 1. short‑dated forwards for near cashflows, 2. selectively executed collars for forecasted receipts, and 3. natural offsets within regional cash pools. Quarterly review on 15 Jul 2026 will reassess hedge ratios.

In liquidity stress testing, base and adverse scenarios maintain acceptable headroom; in the Severe scenario the projected minimum liquidity headroom is USD 45.0m on 05 Sep 2026. Contingency triggers include RCF draw to pre‑empt shortfalls, suspension of discretionary cash outflows, and accelerated receivables collection. Actions are sequenced with governance oversight by the CFO and treasury committee and external counterparties.

structure.heading: Q3 2026 Cash Position Outlook and Short‑Term Funding Plan
text_content: **Q3 2026 Cash Position Outlook and Short‑Term Funding Plan**

As of 30 June 2026 the Group's cash and cash equivalents total USD 312.4m, reported on a consolidated basis and held primarily in U.S. dollar‑denominated demand deposits and money market instruments. These balances are available for immediate use and are concentrated across the principal banking counterparties used by Group Treasury to ensure operational access and intraday liquidity. Short‑term placements and sweep arrangements account for a modest portion of the total; unrestricted cash forms the majority, while restricted balances related to escrow and collateral are monitored separately and excluded from day‑to‑day cash deployment.

The short‑term cash forecast for Q3 2026 identifies a lowest single‑day projected balance of USD 185.0m on 22 August 2026. This point estimate will be tracked through daily forecasting and intraday reporting to the Group CFO and Treasury desk, with variance analysis performed weekly. The USD 185.0m low represents approximately 59.2% of the 30 June cash position and informs timing for funding actions and payment sequencing. Receipts from customers, scheduled tax payments, and planned intercompany movements are the principal drivers of the intra‑quarter trough and will be reviewed regularly thereafter.

Planned short‑term funding for Q3 2026 includes issuing USD 150.0m of 90‑day commercial paper on 15 July 2026 to replenish transactional balances and maintain the intended liquidity buffer. The issuance is scheduled through the existing dealer panel and will be priced competitively in the primary CP market with settlement on issuance date; proceeds will be available immediately for deployment. Contingency measures if market access is impaired include temporary working‑capital measures, timing of discretionary payments, and activation of internal cash concentration mechanics to preserve the forecasted minimum balance and covenant headroom.
